h1: The 6 Best Zero Gravity Camping Chairs of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Zero Gravity Camping Chairs: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 zero gravity camping chairs scored on weight rating, folded size, recline lock and padding, from 250 lb sets to a 500 lb chair.
summary: The Portal Portable Zero Gravity Chair is the best for actual camping: it lists a 20.6 lb weight, a folded size of 42 by 8 inches and a 350 lb rating, which gives you the numbers needed to pack a car. The Suteck is the oversized choice at 500 lb with a 33 inch seat. The NEWBULIG is the budget pick with a removable cushion and a 440 lb rating, and Sweetcrispy sells two light chairs as a set.
intro: Zero gravity chairs borrow a posture from aerospace seating: reclined far enough that your legs sit above your heart, so weight spreads across your back. That is a lovely way to spend an evening at a campsite, but only if the chair survives the trip. A chair that weighs 20 lb, folds to an awkward shape or has a flimsy lock is the one that stays in the garage after the first outing.

We ranked six chairs for camping, reading dimensions and ratings in the listings. Weight rating comes first, since the lock and frame carry the whole load, then chair weight and folded size for hauling, recline range, frame tubing and padding. Where a listing is vague on the numbers a camper cares about, we marked it down.

products.name: Portal Portable Zero Gravity Chair, 350 lb
products.verdict: The clearest dimensions and a compact fold for packing a car, with a 350 lb rating.
products.description:
The Portal lists a 350 lb weight rating, a 20.6 lb chair weight, a 0 to 170 degree lock, a set-up size of 18.5 by 22 by 45.5 inches, a folded size of 42 by 8 inches and a 21 inch seat height.

It ranks first because camping is about packing, and this is the only chair here that tells you every dimension you need to plan the trunk. The 21 inch seat height is easier to climb out of than the lowest chairs. It gives up the Suteck's capacity but is more portable.

Buy it for car camping where packing space is tight. The caveat is that 20.6 lb is heavier than the Sweetcrispy's 15.43 lb, and the $50 to $100 price is not cheap.
cons: 350 lb limit below the oversized chairs
products.idealFor: Car campers who need exact folded dimensions.
products.skipIf: You are over 300 lb or need an oversized seat.

products.name: Suteck Oversized Zero Gravity Chair, 500 lb
products.verdict: The highest rating, the widest seat and a deep-groove lock, in a heavy-duty frame.
products.description:
The Suteck is rated for 500 lb with a 33 inch XXL seat width, 40mm (1.6 inch) steel tubing, a 4 inch removable cushion and an 8mm deep-groove lock covering 90 to 170 degrees.

It ranks second because it is the strongest chair here by every figure that matters for a heavier camper: capacity, frame thickness and lock depth. It loses top spot because the listing does not state chair weight or folded size, which is vital for packing a car. It is also the priciest, at $100 to $200.

Buy it if you are a larger camper who wants the widest seat. The caveat is that the weight and folded size are not given, so expect a large, heavy bundle.
products.idealFor: Larger campers who want the highest rating and widest seat.
products.skipIf: Packing space is tight or you want the lightest chair.

products.name: NEWBULIG Zero Gravity Chair, 440 lb
products.verdict: A 440 lb rating, removable cushion and no assembly, in the $25 to $50 bucket.
products.description:
NEWBULIG offers a 440 lb weight rating, a 90 to 170 degree lock, a removable padded cushion, no assembly and a quick fold, with a cup holder pillow and trays as extras.

It ranks third because it combines a high rating with the lowest price tier, $25 to $50, and a removable cushion that you can wash or leave at home to save space. It trails the Portal on listed dimensions, since folded size and chair weight are not given.

Buy it for heavier campers who want a one-person chair on a budget. The caveat is that the recline starts at 90 degrees, so it does not lie as flat as the 0 degree chairs.
products.idealFor: Heavier campers who want a one-person chair on a budget.

products.name: Colegence Oversized Zero Gravity Chair, 400 lb
products.verdict: A 29 inch seat with 300 gsm padding and a thin 4.9 inch folded profile.
products.description:
The Colegence lists a 400 lb rating, a 29 inch wide seat, 300 gsm padding, 600D Oxford fabric and a folded size of 33.3 by 29.5 by 4.9 inches.

It ranks fourth because the padding makes it the plushest of the lot, while the thin fold slides flat behind a car seat. Its folded footprint is wide, though, at 33.3 by 29.5 inches, which is less convenient than the Portal's narrow 42 by 8 inch roll. It also lacks a stated chair weight.

Buy it for a roomy, well padded seat with a side table and a flat fold. The caveat is the lack of a weight figure and the wide footprint.
products.idealFor: Campers who want a roomy, well padded seat and a flat fold.
products.skipIf: You carry the chair a long way and weight matters.

products.name: Sweetcrispy Zero Gravity Chairs Set of 2
products.verdict: Two matching chairs at 15.43 lb each, rated 330 lb, with a 0 to 160 degree lock.
products.description:
Sweetcrispy sells two chairs, each weighing 15.43 lb with a 330 lb rating, a 0 to 160 degree recline lock and an anti-abrasion, tear-resistant fabric.

It ranks fifth because the set price covers two chairs, which makes the per-seat cost low in the $50 to $100 bucket. At 15.43 lb each, it is the lightest chair here, which makes the long walk to a campsite easier. Its recline stops at 160 degrees, ten short of the 170 degree chairs.

Buy it for a camping couple or family who want two matching chairs. The caveat is that the listing gives no folded size or seat width.
products.idealFor: Camping couples or families who want two light matching chairs.
products.skipIf: You need a rating above 330 lb.

products.award: Best Clear Specs for a Pair
products.name: Best Choice Products Zero Gravity Chairs Set of 2
products.verdict: Two simple chairs with trays and a clearly listed folded size, but a 250 lb rating.
products.description:
Best Choice Products sells two chairs rated 250 lb each, with trays, a textilene fabric, an open size of 32.5 to 61 by 25 by 33.5 to 44 inches and a folded size of 38 by 25 by 6 inches.

It ranks last because the 250 lb rating is the lowest here, so it leaves little margin for heavier campers. The folded size is clearly listed, which helps with packing, and the textilene fabric is wear-resistant. The Sweetcrispy pair offers a higher rating at a similar price.

Buy it for lighter campers who want two simple chairs with trays. The caveat is the rating, which is 80 lb below the Sweetcrispy.
products.idealFor: Lighter campers who want two simple chairs with trays.
products.skipIf: You weigh over 200 lb and want a margin.

whatMatters.detail: The rating is the load the frame and lock are built to carry, and a chair loaded near its limit wears out quickly. Pick a rating well above your weight, with margin for a bag or a child on your lap. Check the per-chair rating on set listings, since a set of two can hide a low number.

Camping is mostly carrying, so a chair that weighs 15 lb is far easier to walk to a site than one that weighs 25 lb. Folded size tells you whether it fits in a trunk or behind a seat. Look for both numbers on the listing, and be cautious where only one is given, since a chair that hides its weight is usually not the lightest in its class.

True zero gravity needs a deep recline with the legs raised, and a lock holds the angle you choose. A range of 0 to 170 degrees gives more positions than 90 to 170, and a deep-groove lock grips firmly. Look for the stated range and a lock description, not a general claim of zero gravity.

Seat width decides whether larger campers sit comfortably, and padding decides how long the chair stays comfortable. A 33 inch seat suits oversized users, while a 29 inch seat is roomy for most. Check the stated width and a padding figure such as 300 gsm, and see if the cushion removes, because a removable cushion can be dried or washed after a damp weekend.

Thick steel tubing, such as 40mm, resists bending under load, and tear-resistant fabric like 600D Oxford or textilene resists snags and UV. Cheap thin frames sag and fabric splits at the seams. Look for a stated tubing thickness and a named fabric, and avoid listings that mention only a strong frame, since without a figure there is nothing to compare between brands.

faq.q: Will these fit in a small car?
faq.a: Check folded size. The Portal folds to 42 by 8 inches and the Colegence to 4.9 inches thick. The Suteck and NEWBULIG do not list a folded size, so measure your trunk against the product page first.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Buying a set without checking the per-chair rating. The Best Choice Products pair is rated 250 lb each, and the Sweetcrispy 330 lb. A heavier camper should look at the NEWBULIG or Suteck.

faq.q: Is a zero gravity chair worth it over a folding chair?
faq.a: For evening camps, yes. The recline on the Portal or Sweetcrispy supports the back and lifts the legs, while a folding chair sits upright. For quick tasks, an upright chair is lighter to carry.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Unfold it, lock the side arms and slide into the recline you want. The NEWBULIG needs no assembly and folds in seconds. Check the lock is engaged on the Suteck before sitting.

faq.q: How do I look after it?
faq.a: Wipe the fabric clean and let it dry fully before packing, which prevents mildew. Check the lock and joints before each trip. The Colegence's thick padding and the NEWBULIG's removable cushion should be dried separately.

faq.q: Can I use one on soft ground?
faq.a: Yes, but the feet sink in sand or mud. The Suteck's wide frame helps, and a flat board under each foot spreads the load. Always check that the lock is fully engaged on uneven terrain.

finalTake: Buy the Portal if you pack a car and want exact numbers: 350 lb, 20.6 lb and a 42 by 8 inch fold. Choose the Suteck for oversized comfort at 500 lb, and the NEWBULIG as the budget 440 lb option. The Sweetcrispy pair is the lightest set. Whichever you pick, check the per-chair rating.
